The augmentation system would be capable of delivering flows of up to 15 cfs, an amount that would more than restore Howard Creek to preproject base flow levels. The use of this system would be dependent upon the quality of the water available in the upper reservoir to use for augmentation.
Environmental studies of streams in the project area have been conducted by Applicant in the areas of hydrology, water quality, benthos, amphibians and reptiles, geology, and recreation and esthetics. An analysis of the Howar. Creek fishery has been made by the South Carolina Department of Wildlife and Marine Resources. Wildlife and botanical studies have also been made by the Applicant. Applicant has sponsored a number of studies of Howard Creek basin in preparation for the development of the proposed Project (Section 2.2.2.2). Applicant has also sponsored or conducted studies of the effect of pumped storage on Lake Jocassee and the trout resources of Howard Creek (Appendices J and K, Exhibit W). Applicant is conducting a study on the vertical distribution of fishes in Lake Jocassee.
Applicant proposes to establish a water quality monitoring program in Howard Creek sufficient to detect any major trends above and below the project area. This program would continue into the operational phase of the proposed project. A benthic sampling program would also be established and conducted in Howard Creek during construction and early operation of the project. The program would planned to detect changes in the benthic community above and below the project area.
Studies are proposed by the Applicant to evaluate the benefits that natural seepage through the dams may provide for Howard Creek. Such seepage could serve as a supplemental source of high quality water for the stream. The Applicant expects the amount of seepage to be about 2 to 5 cfs.
The Applicant has water quality monitoring stations at several locations on Lake Jocassee and has installed a continuous temperature recorder in the vicinity of Jocassee Dam. Such monitoring would continue through the construction and early operational stages of the project to provide data on the operational effects of the Jocassee pumped storage project and the Bad Creek Project on Lake Jocassee.
